steps.description: Using the filtered counts and aligned metadata from T1S1, fit DESeq2 with design ~ batch + condition, setting control as the reference level of condition so the reported contrast is treated vs control. Use the Wald test with default independent filtering and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Produce the full result table for every tested gene with baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, and a shrunken log2 fold change from apeglm (fall back to ashr if the coefficient shape prevents apeglm) for effect-size ranking. Report the number of genes at padj < 0.05, split by direction, and also at padj < 0.05 combined with |shrunken log2FC| > 1. Report the estimated batch coefficient's influence: refit the identical model without the batch term (~ condition), and report the number of significant genes under each model, the overlap, and the Spearman correlation of the test statistics between models — do not present the no-batch fit as the primary result. Do not filter the ranked list to significant genes before GSEA; GSEA requires the full ranking
Background universe for ORA is the set of genes tested by DESeq2, not all 12,000 input genes and not the whole genome

steps.description: Take the full DESeq2 result table from T1S2 (all tested genes, ~ batch + condition design) and run gene set enrichment on a ranked list built from the Wald statistic (or -log10(p) signed by the shrunken log2FC if the statistic is unavailable), against human gene sets: the hallmark collection and the GO Biological Process collection, both of which the environment holds for Homo sapiens keyed on HGNC symbols — matching this dataset's gene-symbol identifiers directly, so no ID conversion should be needed. Resolve these references at run time by what they are (human hallmark sets; human GO BP sets) rather than by a hardcoded path. Use fgsea with an explicit permutation/eps setting, minimum set size 15 and maximum 500, BH FDR. Report the leading-edge genes for every set at padj < 0.05 and produce a bar or dot plot of the top enriched sets by normalised enrichment score, separately for hallmark and GO BP. Because GO BP is a nested hierarchy with heavily overlapping sets, collapse redundant significant sets (fgsea collapsePathways or an overlap-based grouping) before reporting a count, and report both the raw and collapsed counts. Additionally run an over-representation test on the padj < 0.05 DESeq2 gene set against the same collections, using the tested gene set as the background universe, and note where GSEA and ORA disagree. If either gene set collection is unavailable at run time, run against whichever is present and state clearly in the output which collection was missing and that coverage is therefore partial.

Human (not mouse or rat) gene set collections are used, and the collections actually loaded are named in the output with their set counts
Fraction of the ranked gene symbols that matched each collection is reported
Enriched sets at padj < 0.05 are reported with NES, size, padj and leading-edge genes, written to disk
GO BP significant sets are collapsed for redundancy and both raw and collapsed counts are reported
ORA results on the significant gene list use the tested genes as background universe, and GSEA-vs-ORA disagreements are noted

plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE, batch in model
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a small bulk RNA-seq experiment: raw salmon gene-level integer counts for 12,000 gene symbols across 12 human kidney samples (counts.csv, 12000 x 13 with the gene symbol in column 1), plus metadata.csv (12 x 3) giving condition (6 treated vs 6 control) and a two-level processing batch that is balanced across conditions. Because batch is balanced and not confounded with condition, the correct handling is to include it as a covariate in the design (~ batch + condition) rather than to remove it from the counts before testing — removing it first would understate residual variance and inflate significance. T1S1 does QC and design verification: library-size and detection summaries, filtering of low-count genes, VST, PCA and sample correlation coloured by condition and batch, and an explicit cross-tabulation confirming the 3/3 balance in each batch, so the reader knows how much variance batch actually explains before any test. T1S2 runs the DESeq2 negative-binomial Wald test on raw counts with ~ batch + condition, treated vs control, with shrunken log2 fold changes, and reports the full result table plus the significant set at FDR < 0.05; it also refits without the batch term as a sensitivity check so the effect of the covariate on the gene ranking is quantified rather than asserted. T1S3 is a limma-voom replication on the same design, used purely as a method-robustness check — with n=6 per arm, agreement between two independent frameworks is the strongest available evidence that a call is not an artefact of one dispersion model. T2S1 takes the DESeq2 ranked list into gene-set enrichment against the staged human hallmark and GO Biological Process collections, which match this dataset's organism and HGNC symbol space. The plan makes no claim about the treatment's identity or mechanism — the metadata only labels treated/control — so interpretation stops at which genes and which processes move.
